title: Week Summary: Scope, Context, and System Boundaries

concepts.name: System boundary
concepts.description: The line separating the system under design from users, external systems, and environmental dependencies.

concepts.name: System context
concepts.description: The external setting of a system, including actors, neighboring systems, interfaces, assumptions, and constraints.

concepts.name: External dependency
concepts.description: A person, organization, system, service, data source, or platform outside the system boundary that affects behavior.

concepts.name: Trust boundary
concepts.description: A boundary where data or control crosses between zones with different levels of trust or authority.

concepts.name: Architecture scope
concepts.description: The span of system, organization, lifecycle, and decision-making concerns covered by an architecture effort.

concepts.name: Responsibility boundary
concepts.description: A boundary that clarifies which element, team, or party owns a capability or decision.

concepts.name: Ownership model
concepts.description: The assignment of responsibility for architectural elements, decisions, operations, and change.

concepts.name: Scope creep
concepts.description: Expansion of expected responsibility beyond the agreed system boundary or architecture goal.

concepts.name: Architecture assumption
concepts.description: A belief about context, usage, technology, organization, or environment that influences architectural decisions.

concepts.name: Environmental constraint
concepts.description: A condition outside the system that restricts acceptable architecture choices.

concepts.name: Assumption validation
concepts.description: The process of checking whether important architecture assumptions are true enough to rely on.

concepts.name: Integration risk
concepts.description: Risk caused by uncertain behavior at interfaces with external systems, services, teams, or data sources.
